To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the configuration interaction (CI) model is an excellent tool for describing the properties of atomic nuclei, and (ii) the CI model with the energy density functional (EDF) monopole corrections provides a new way to construct a Hamiltonian for CI calculations that can be used in a variety of applications.

(1) the method of constraining configuration interaction calculations to the energy of spherical configurations obtained from EDF calculations is a viable method for obtaining energy spectra in medium-mass nuclei; (2) the method is applicable to any renormalized interaction; and (3) the three-body terms that are necessary to achieve good saturation properties are obtained directly from the EDF.

we present a method for constructing a nuclear Hamiltonian that reproduces the binding energies of spherical configurations from energy-density-functional (e.g., Skyrme-Hartree-Fock) methods in the limit of one Slater determinant, but can also reproduce the energies and wave functions of the ground states and low-lying collective states of nuclei with a renormalized nucleonic interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of nuclear properties of the atomic nucleus using the nuclear shell model, which is the best available microscopic model of nuclear structure.
the development of a new method for constructing an effective Hamiltonian for configuration-interaction calculations with constraints to energy-density-functional binding energies.

the development of a unified model for nuclear structure calculations that can be used in the limit of a single Slater determinant for the description of the nuclear ground state and for the description of excited states and correlation energies with a renormalized nucleons-nucleon interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new model, which is based on the EDF, is a good starting point for configuration interaction calculations in medium-mass nuclei.
the present approach is a promising method for obtaining a Hamiltonian with realistic nucleon-nucleus interactions, but that it requires further development.

, although the present method does not yet provide an optimal description of the nuclear ground states, it is very encouraging that the present approach provides a unified description of nuclear ground-state properties and spectra, with the correct asymptotic behavior and with no additional parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method presented here can be used for obtaining accurate nuclear spectra and correlation energies in the region of the doubly magic nucleus 132Sn and for nuclei close to it.
the EDFs can be used to construct a Hamiltonian for the configuration interaction calculations with the renormalized nucleons.

the present approach is an efficient method of obtaining a Hamiltonian for the calculation of energy spectra of deformed nuclei with the constraint that the energy of a spherical configuration is equal to the corresponding EDF value.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a configuration-interaction (CI) method with constraints to energies obtained with an EDF can be used to obtain a Hamiltonian that is capable of producing good results for both binding energies and spectra.
the EDFs can be used to construct a Hamiltonian for correlated calculations, which allows one to use the EDFs in a wider range of applications.
a configuration-interaction (CI) calculation with a constrained Hamiltonian can reproduce both the EDF binding energies and the CI energy spectrum.
